mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the 5-year moving average coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its 5-week simple moving average
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day forward returns remain positive despite trigger activation, or FEDFUNDS momentum fades before SPX reaction.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 5% for two consecutive months, labor market strength prompts firms to increase capital expenditures, boosting equity valuations and driving positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses below 50,000 monthly average for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 60 days, the 20-day forward return is negative despite sustained PAYEMS declines below 50k, or other macro indicators contradict labor strength.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals deflationary pressure, which reduces real discount rates and produces negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls for three consecutive months by >0.2pp
failure_condition: Over 12 months, the 60-day forward return remains positive despite repeated CPIAUCSL declines >0.2pp, or alternative inflation proxies contradict CPIAUCSL pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average coincides with supply-chain easing, lowering component costs and prompting positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above its 12-month simple moving average
failure_condition: Over 60 days, 20-day forward returns remain flat or negative despite INDPRO stays above its 12-month SMA, or other supply indicators show contraction.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below the 10-year average, the market anticipates prolonged easing, which amplifies equity valuation growth and yields a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: 3-month FEDFUNDS SMA falls below 10-year FEDFUNDS SMA
failure_condition: Across multiple 60-day windows, 60-day forward returns fail to outperform a baseline of 0.5% monthly SPX return, or FEDFUNDS re-enters restrictive zone before effect materializes.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in job openings (RSAFS) above 7 million coincides with hiring acceleration, strengthening consumer demand and producing a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS crosses above 7,000,000 for a single month
failure_condition: Over 60 days, 20-day forward returns remain negative despite persistent RSAFS >7m, or other labor indicators (e.g., PAYEMS) contradict hiring surge.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in unemployment (PAYEMS) and inflation (CPIAUCSL) below their respective 50th percentile thresholds indicate a dual labor-supply shock that amplifies equity risk appetite and drives a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < median PAYEMS and CPIAUCSL < median CPIAUCSL in the same month
failure_condition: Over 60 days, the interaction signal recurs but produces no statistically significant positive 20-day forward returns (p > 0.05), or alternative shocks negate the combined effect.

mechanism_narrative: During a prolonged period of falling consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) without a corresponding rise in wage growth (UNRATE), the market interprets deflation as structural, depressing discount rates and producing negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL declines for 4 consecutive months while UNRATE remains below 4% for the same period
failure_condition: Over 60 days, the 20-day forward return is positive despite repeated CPIAUCSL declines and UNRATE stagnation, or wage growth eventually offsets CPI declines.
